questiontext.text:
Consider the matrix \(A\) and the column vector \(\mathbf{x}\):

\[ A = {@MM@} \qquad \mathbf{x} = {@vv@} \]

Compute the matrix–vector product \(A\mathbf{x}\), if it is defined. If the product is not defined, enter the zero vector to indicate this.

(The answer box has the same number of rows as \(A\).)

\( A\mathbf{x} = \) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
[[ if test="is(ddef=1)" ]]

The product is defined: \(A\) is \({@m@}\times{@n@}\) and \(\mathbf{x}\) is \({@n@}\times 1\). Because the number of columns of \(A\) equals the number of entries of \(\mathbf{x}\), the product is defined and the result is \({@m@}\times 1\).

Multiply each row of \(A\) by the column \(\mathbf{x}\): multiply entries in matching positions and add. Writing the working inside the result vector:

\[ A\mathbf{x} = {@MM@}\,{@vv@} = {@ta@}. \] [[/ if ]][[ if test="is(ddef=0)" ]]

The product is not defined.

\(A\) is \({@m@}\times{@n@}\), so it has \({@n@}\) columns, while \(\mathbf{x}\) has \({@p@}\) entries (it is \({@p@}\times 1\)).

For \(A\mathbf{x}\) to be defined, the number of columns of \(A\) must equal the number of entries of \(\mathbf{x}\). Here \({@n@}\neq{@p@}\), so the product cannot be formed. We signal this by entering the zero vector.

[[/ if ]]

node.description: Correct: A.x (or the zero vector when undefined)

truefeedback.text: This product is defined: \(A\) has \({@n@}\) columns and \(\mathbf{x}\) has \({@n@}\) entries, and these match. So work it out rather than entering the zero vector.

truefeedback.text: Not quite. Multiply each row of \(A\) by \(\mathbf{x}\): multiply entries in matching positions and add. Check your arithmetic against the worked solution.

falsefeedback.text: This product is not defined: \(A\) has \({@n@}\) columns but \(\mathbf{x}\) has \({@p@}\) entries. The product \(A\mathbf{x}\) only exists when these are equal. Enter the zero vector to indicate that it is not defined.
